I'll add one test that reads the four templates, extracts each triage block, and requires them to be identical. This is a case where the text is the contract, so asserting on the file text is appropriate.

<edit path="tests/test_issue_templates.py">
import re
from pathlib import Path

TEMPLATE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / ".github" / "ISSUE_TEMPLATE"
TEMPLATES = ["bug.md", "feature.md", "question.md", "docs.md"]
TRIAGE_BLOCK = re.compile(r"<!-- triage: begin -->.*?<!-- triage: end -->", re.DOTALL)


def test_triage_blocks_are_identical_across_templates():
    blocks = {
        name: TRIAGE_BLOCK.findall((TEMPLATE_DIR / name).read_text())
        for name in TEMPLATES
    }

    for name, found in blocks.items():
        assert len(found) == 1, f"{name} has {len(found)} triage blocks, expected 1"

    reference = blocks["bug.md"][0]
    drifted = [name for name in TEMPLATES if blocks[name][0] != reference]
    assert not drifted, f"triage block differs from bug.md in: {drifted}"
</edit>

Next I run the new test on its own. If the templates are currently in sync, it will pass, which tells me nothing yet about whether it can fail.

<command>
uv run pytest tests/test_issue_templates.py -v
</command>

To watch it fail, I introduce drift in a throwaway way: back up `feature.md`, change its priority line, run the test, and restore the file regardless of the result. I would first look at the file's triage block to confirm the `sed` pattern matches.

<command>
cp .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md /tmp/feature.md.bak \
  && sed -i '' 's/\*\*Priority:\*\* p3/**Priority:** p1/' .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md; \
uv run pytest tests/test_issue_templates.py -v; \
cp /tmp/feature.md.bak .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md \
  && diff /tmp/feature.md.bak .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.md && echo restored
</command>

I expect that run to fail with `triage block differs from bug.md in: ['feature.md']`. That is the right failure, since it comes from the drift and not from a typo or a missing file. The `diff` confirms the template is back to its original content.

Last, I run the project's documented suite to check the rest of the tests still pass.

<command>
uv run pytest -q
</command>

The failure message names the drifted files.

- **Plain run:** this likely passes, since last month's drift was presumably fixed.
- **Red check:** to confirm the test can fail, I temporarily change the priority in `feature.md`, run the test, and restore the file from a backup. I expect it to fail naming `feature.md`.
- **Full suite:** `uv run pytest -q`. I'll report any failures by name, including ones I didn't cause.

One thing to be aware of: `bug.md` is the reference, so if the intended source of truth is a different template, say so and I'll change it. The comparison is exact, so whitespace differences count as drift.
